section_title: Why does Paul ask the church to welcome Phoebe?

versions.label: BSB
paragraphs: 1 I commend to you our sister Phoebe, a servant of the church in Cenchrea. 2 Welcome her in the Lord in a manner worthy of the saints, and assist her with anything she may need from you. For she has been a great help to many people, including me.

context_lines: Paul commends Phoebe as a sister and a servant of the church in Cenchrea. He asks the Roman believers to receive her in a way worthy of God’s people and to help her with whatever she needs.

The word translated servant is diakonos (dee-AH-koh-noss), διάκονος. Its range includes servant, minister and deacon; see [Thayer’s entry](https://biblehub.com/greek/1249.htm). Paul identifies her service with a particular church and honors the help she has given to many, including himself.

The request makes mutual care practical. Someone who has supported others is now to receive support from another community. Paul’s commendation calls the church to recognize her service and act on that recognition.
common_interpretation_lines: Christians commonly recognize this as a commendation of Phoebe’s important service and a call to welcome and assist her. [Wesley’s note on verse 1](https://wesley.nnu.edu/john-wesley/john-wesleys-notes-on-the-bible/notes-on-st-pauls-epistle-to-the-romans/) understands her role as that of a deaconess, and [Calvin’s comment](https://biblehub.com/commentaries/calvin/romans/16.htm) also treats it as recognized service in the church. The passage identifies her work and the response it deserves without describing an appointment ceremony or a complete set of duties.
god_plan_lines: [1 Peter 4:10–11](https://biblehub.com/bsb/1_peter/4.htm) calls each believer to use God’s gifts in service to others, with the strength He provides and for His glory through Christ. Phoebe’s commendation gives a concrete example of service being recognized and supported within God’s people.

The movement between communities also matters: care is not confined to people already familiar to the receiving church. Shared belonging in the Lord becomes a reason to welcome and help a sister whose work has benefited others.
current_position_lines: We don't have a position on this passage yet. When our study reaches a conclusion the text supports, it will appear here.
